claims.claim: Smallmouth nest success (the share of nests producing swim-up fry) is 44-96 % in lakes with a median near 75 % across 26 studies
claims.source_value: Table 4 lists 27 site-years from 10 published sources plus Steinhart's own Lake Erie and unpublished Opeongo data, 21-96 % of nests reaching the free-swimming larval stage. Lakes alone (23 rows) also span 21-96 % (Lake Erie, Ohio, 21-41 %; Lake Erie, Ontario, 1982 and Lake Huron 1974, 33 %), median 55-63 % (depending on how Lake Opinicon's 44-63 % range is counted); all 27 rows, median 58-63 %. The source states no '44-96 %', no median and no '26 studies'
claims.quote: Nebish Lake, Wisconsin 1985 49 96% … Lake Erie, Ohio 2000 47 21%
claims.conditions: endpoint: % of nests reaching the free-swimming, larval stage; N = 13-1,864 nests per row; lakes and rivers in Ontario, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Maine and Virginia
claims.note: Table read on the page image. The research note behind the sentence says the table's layout was 'garbled in extraction'. Medians are the reader's count from the table (lakes: 21, 23, 33, 33, 41, 44-63, 45, 47, 50, 54, 54, 55, 67, 75, 77, 79, 82, 85, 87, 87, 88, 93, 96; rivers: 43, 58, 64, 84). Leaving out Steinhart's own Lake Erie, Ohio values, lakes run 33-96 % with a median of about 71 %. Suggested wording: 'from 21 to 96 % of nests reached the free-swimming stage in 27 site-years compiled by Steinhart (2004), half of them below about 60 %'.

claims.claim: Storms destroyed nests at 0.015 per day at Opeongo and 0.065 per day in Lake Erie
claims.location: p. 118 (PDF p. 140), chapter 6 methods; Table 7, p. 132 (PDF p. 154)
claims.quote: Base pS values were 0.065 in Lake Erie and 0.015 in Lake Opeongo
claims.conditions: daily probability that a nest was destroyed by a storm, estimated by the Mayfield method from nests monitored in situ in Lakes Erie and Opeongo (G. B. Steinhart, unpublished data); used as base values in a dynamic programming model
claims.note: the same values are Table 2 of Steinhart et al. 2008 (Evol. Ecol. Res. 10: 351-371), which could be cited instead of the dissertation

notes: Table 4 also lists South Branch Lake, Maine, at 88 % (1972, N = 26) and 67 % (1971, N = 15) from Neves (1975), whereas the paper (§3.6.2, from Neves's abstract) gives 67 % and 77 %: check Neves_1975. Within Steinhart's own Lake Erie study, control nests succeeded at 29.8 % against 11.4 % (angled, no predators) and 14.0 % (angled, with predators) (p. 81). The model's base daily survival for guarded offspring is 0.90 (embryos) and 0.92 (larvae) (Table 7), the values the paper credits to Steinhart et al. 2008.
